findings.finding: The new Lead capture accepts U+2028/U+2029 and firstBullet's trim() strips them, so a Lead line with a leading or trailing U+2028 lists and countersigns as the bare lead id. Not a forgery: identity is the lead the line names and the daemon writes it. Breaks the fail-closed symmetry for the identity field. Server and client match.
findings.suggestion: Follow-up: trim only space/tab in firstBullet (both mirrors) and add a corpus case expecting such an entry unlisted. Leadwright S1-E rejection in the contract covers it upstream.

findings.finding: Display only, WebUI-form entries: under the multiline flag, anchors also match at a lone CR, U+2028 and U+2029, so the shown evidence can differ. Predates the change; does not affect what is listed or countersigned.
findings.suggestion: Follow-up: build the WebUI-form evidence from a newline split plus the non-multiline bullet regex.

code.reviewer_notes: Verdict: no HIGH or MEDIUM remains. Server and client regexes byte-identical, linear, tests real (the U+2028/U+2029 and empty-value cases fail under the old captures), lone CR fails closed and is pinned, no empty Lead can be listed or countersigned, consumers of the capture still work, whole-PR pass found no HIGH. Earlier rounds on this PR (four code reviews, three doubt reviews) fixed fence-masking forgery paths, logged-kind phantom ADR numbering, unprotected WebUI-form and marker-above header owners, and three classes of regex slowdown and empty-value poisoning.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a forged entry can never be listed — An evidence value containing a line break followed by a WebUI-form header after a LISTED marker-owned entry can still list a marker-less header.

Claim under doubt: countersign is local to the two files — The daemon's dedup scans only decisions-proposed.md, so a countersigned decisionKey is accepted again, and its marker regex is looser than the reader's.
Claim under doubt: fail-closed costs only the offending entry — A dangling fence opener written via a line break in evidence poisons every later entry silently, with no UI or server signal.
Claim under doubt: legacy entries behave as before — Legacy WebUI entries with structural lines in their body are now unlisted; the logged header regex accepts 4 or more digits.

The comment claims a leadless daemon entry's text "is still part of the byte range … so countersigning another entry never moves or removes it." That is false: the skipped head still participates as a block delimiter — the previous listed entry's `endIndex` is the next head's `startIndex` (not the next listed head's), so the leadless entry's entire text sits inside the previous entry's `block` and is spliced out when that entry is countersigned. Silent deletion of daemon data, contradicting both the inline invariant and the contract doc's framing.
findings.suggestion: Either change the delimiter so a leadless head terminates the previous entry's block (leaving its text in place), or fix the comment and document the deletion behavior in the contract doc. Pick one and test it.

findings.finding: If a daemon entry's fence is unclosed (truncated quote, partial write under the lock), `daemonTail` returns the whole block, so a forged `- Lead: evil-lead` bullet inside the quote wins the identity lookup — exactly the injection the module header claims is defended. The fenced-set used for header detection also leaves such lines unfenced, so a forged header inside an unclosed quote would split the entry too.
findings.suggestion: Decide and test a policy for unclosed fences (e.g., treat the whole rest of the entry as quoted / reject the entry), rather than silently falling back to the insecure path.

findings.finding: The acceptance criterion says the sample is "pinned as a fixture in both repositories," but this diff only pins it in the WebUI repo. The leadwright copy (and the hash-equality test against it) is described as a future obligation ("must be pinned in leadwright … unit S1-E"); nothing in this change verifies it. The WebUI-side hash test only checks the fixture against this repo's own doc, so the cross-repo gate is not actually enforced yet.
findings.suggestion: If S1-E is genuinely a separate unit in the leadwright repo, note the AC as partially met; otherwise add the second pinned copy / cross-check now.

findings.finding: The client test reads the fixture via a relative path out of `client/` into `server/`. If the two packages are ever built/tested in isolation (client-only CI checkout, published client package), this test fails at file-read time, not assertion time — a brittle coupling that the "no cross-package import" rule elsewhere in the codebase argues against.
findings.suggestion: Copy the fixture into `client/…/__tests__/fixtures/` and assert its SHA-256 equals the contract doc's hash, mirroring the server-side gate instead of reaching across directories.

findings.finding: The "crash residue" test doesn't actually simulate the crash state it names: it rewrites the whole sample file (both entries) after a successful countersign, which is indistinguishable from a fresh duplicate of entry 2 as well. It does validate the retry identity for entry 1, but the residue-vs-duplicate discrimination (`bodyAfterHeader` comparison) is only exercised on the matching-text path via `performCountersign`; the `toLoggedBlock`-normalized comparison for a daemon-form residue where the logged block and re-proposed block differ only in trailing whitespace is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add a case where the residual proposed block has a trailing blank line / CRLF so the `trimEnd()` normalization is what makes the match succeed — otherwise that fix in countersign-core.ts is untested.

findings.finding: headerOf` re-derives the marker/lead independently of `parseProposedEntries` and uses slightly different rules (no `fenced` check on the marker line; blank-tolerance re-implemented). For blocks coming from `parseProposedEntries` these agree today, but `toLoggedBlock` is also called from the countersign duplicate-identity path on `stillProposed.block` — any future divergence between the two derivations turns a crash-residue retry into a spurious `duplicate_identity` (or vice versa). Worth a shared helper or a cross-check test.
findings.suggestion: Have `parseProposedEntries` carry the parsed header (marker, lead) on the entry so `toLoggedBlock` doesn't re-parse.  Positive notes: the injection tests (forged header/lead inside quote and evidence pointer) are behavioral and would fail against the naive implementation; CRLF, orphan-marker, and mixed-document countersign cases are covered; the hash-gate test tying fixture to contract doc is a good compatibility gate; the `trimEnd()` fix in countersign-core.ts correctly handles the previously-brittle body comparison.  Overall: the core grammar, countersign-once semantics, and injection defence are sound and well-tested, but the leadless-entry deletion contradicts its own stated invariant, the unclosed-fence path undermines the injection guarantee, and the cross-repo half of the "both repositories" AC is not present. Ship-with-fixes.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: Countersigning preserves quoted daemon text verbatim in the log, but `parseLoggedEntries` still treats every matching ADR header as a real entry, including headers inside the quote fence. A proposal quoting `## ADR-9999 [2026-11-20T09:15:00Z] someone` therefore creates a phantom logged entry, inflates subsequent numbering, and can break crash recovery because the real logged block is truncated.
findings.suggestion: Make logged-entry parsing ignore headers inside paired quote fences too. Test countersigning and crash recovery with an ADR-shaped header inside the daemon quote.

findings.finding: The blank-line tolerance test does not modify the fixture: `"-status\n## Proposed"` never occurs because the marker ends with `"-status -->\n## Proposed"`. The client test has the same mistake, so both pass without exercising the claimed behavior.
findings.suggestion: Replace the actual marker/header boundary and assert that the modified input contains the added blank line before parsing.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The supplied diff covers both header forms, but logged parsing needs matching fence handling; workspace access was blocked, so I could not read the referenced brief or run tests.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
